subject: Where LLM traffic runs & delete guarantees — follow up
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@mediconnect.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@mediconnect.io
Date: Tue, 19 Nov 2024 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency + deletion Qs before eval

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Mediconnect is interested in a short eval but our security team needs clarity on a few things before we proceed. Can you confirm the following at a high level? If you have a one-page that summarizes this, that would be ideal.

1) Where are inference requests executed by default (regions + major subprocessors)? Do you ever route outside the requested region?
2) If data routes across borders, what legal/technical safeguards apply (encryption in transit, subprocessors, contracts)?
3) Default retention for request/response logs, traces, and any user-supplied artifacts (how long are they kept and where)?
4) Deletion guarantees: if we ask you to delete data for a customer, what is the timeline for primary stores, caches, and backups?
5) Evidence: SOC 2 or other compliance docs, and a current subprocessor inventory we can share with procurement.

If easier, happy to set a short call for the security team + your engineer.

Best,
Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Security Engineering
Mediconnect

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hi Alex — great to hear, and thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short summary and the current subprocessor inventory (attached). High level answers below; Ben (cc) can add technical details.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-residency-summary.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv (CSV)]

Quick answers (summary):
- Execution locales: Hosted API defaults to routing requests to the region closest to the request origin; our catalog supports pinned-region endpoints (US / EU / APAC) for customers who require locality. Major subprocessors: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west1), and a few managed telemetry vendors listed in the inventory.
- Cross-border transfers: routing is policy-driven. If a customer pins to EU-only, we will only use EU regions and EU-based subprocessors. Otherwise, requests may transit between regions for routing/fallback. All traffic is TLS encrypted.
- Retention: default operational logs/traces retained 30 days for hosted accounts (used for debugging/ops). Request payloads are transient; we keep them only as needed for live KV cache and for 30 days of debug snapshots unless otherwise configured. Dedicated/Private customers can set their own TTLs.
- Deletion flow: deletion requests cause tombstoning in primary stores within 24 hours; a purge job runs and completes within 72 hours for active storage. Backups and long-term archives are included in the deletion workflow and are scheduled for removal within 30–45 days (we provide attestations once complete).
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II is available under NDA; subprocessor list attached.

Would you like a 30-min call with Ben to walk the team through the diagrams and the timelines? Jordan is on the thread for procurement/next steps.

Thanks,

Hi Alex — following Marissa's summary, a few technical clarifications for your security team. Quoting her note below for context.

On Tue, Nov 19, 2024 at 10:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick answers (summary):
> - Execution locales: Hosted API defaults to routing requests to the region closest to the request origin; our catalog supports pinned-region endpoints (US / EU / APAC) for customers who require locality.

Detailed notes:
- Regional execution & routing: We operate regional clusters (US, EU, APAC). For hosted customers who do not pin a region, requests are routed by latency and capacity. If a request originates from the EU and the EU cluster is healthy, it will be served in EU. If capacity constraints occur, routing falls back to the next closest compatible region (we surface this in the request metadata).
- Subprocessors & data flows: Subprocessor_inventory.csv lists third parties and their processing locations. We have Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with cloud providers and the larger subprocessors; smaller telemetry vendors are covered under SOC2 + contractual clauses.
- Encryption & key control: All in-flight traffic uses TLS. At rest, customer data in hosted services is encrypted with platform-managed keys. For Dedicated customers, you can bring your own KMS; for Private deployments we support customer-managed HSMs.
- Caching & transient state: KV caches are in-memory on the serving nodes and are ephemeral (evicted based on TTL and memory pressure). Persistent artifacts (logs/traces) are written to regional object stores.
- Deletion mechanics: When we receive a deletion request (API or support ticket) we mark the object as deleted (tombstone) in the primary table within 24 hours. An async purge process removes tombstoned records from object stores within 72 hours. Snapshots/backups are rotated and eligible for secure deletion; our current schedule removes data from backups within 30–45 days depending on the backup retention window. We record deletion events and can provide an attestation PDF once purge completes.

Evidence we can provide to a security reviewer (under NDA): SOC 2 Type II report, encryption architecture diagram, subprocessor inventory, and a short deletion attestation template. If you need stronger guarantees, our Private deployment keeps all execution and storage entirely customer-managed on-prem.

Happy to run a short walk-through with our SRE/security lead and show live logs (redacted) and the metadata that indicates execution region for a request.
